Today (17th), a netizen uploaded a video on social media, which appears to be closed-circuit television footage from a back alley. The footage shows three people talking, at least two of whom are clearly wearing Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD) uniforms. According to the FEHD's uniform information, the two are suspected to be a Hawker Control Officer and a Senior Hawker Control Officer.

The clip shows two officer-grade personnel talking in a back alley. One of them first takes out a cigarette and starts smoking, then the Senior Hawker Control Officer steps forward, takes out a cigarette case and a lighter, brushes his hair, puts a cigarette in his mouth, and walks away with his back to the camera, with a wisp of smoke visible nearby.

Captjal Studio (the news outlet) inquired with the FEHD whether the personnel in the clip were staff of the department. The FEHD confirmed in reply that the personnel in the clip were members of the Hawker Control Team under its jurisdiction. A spokesperson said the incident occurred in early June this year. The reporter asked whether FEHD personnel are permitted to smoke while in uniform; if the clip is genuine, whether the personnel has violated regulations, and whether this would affect the department's image. The FEHD replied that according to established departmental regulations, employees are not permitted to smoke while in uniform and in public places.

The FEHD stated that the department attaches great importance to employee discipline and professional conduct, and has initiated a disciplinary investigation into the incident, and will take appropriate action in accordance with established procedures and the investigation results. The spokesperson also pointed out that the department has clear requirements on the conduct of employees while in uniform, and any behavior violating departmental disciplinary regulations will be followed up seriously.
